units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 14:10">Targ. Gen. XIV, 10</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 84a:2">B. Mets. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>אבוך ע׳ … ואת עֲרִיק ללודקיא</he> (Ms. M. <he>ברח</he>) thy father fled (from persecution) to A., flee thou to Laodicea; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 3:4:5">Y. Maasr. III, 50ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>עד דעַרְקַת וכ׳</he> (I shall call thee so,) until thou runnest away and goest &c.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31">Gen. R. s. 31</cite> (<cite ref="P01450"><he>עָרְקִין</he></cite>) <he>עֲרִיקִין הוינן מן קומי וכ׳</he> we were fugitives from a (Roman) troop, and living in &c., v. <cite ref="B00507"><he>בְּטִיטָא</he></cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 1:1:7">Y. Pes. I, beg. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>כד הוינן ערקין וכ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 16a:2">Ab. Zar. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>דכי שלים … מֵעֲרַק עַרְקֵי</he> for when their weapons (missiles) are spent, they run away (and do not attack with their shields).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:7:2">Y. Sabb. XVI, end, 15ᵈ</cite> <he>פריס … ונורא עַרְקָא מינה</he> he spread his cloak …, and the fire fled from it (v. <cite ref="C00219"><he>גָּדִישָׁא</he></cite>); a. fr.—[<cite ref="Gittin 78a">Gitt. 78ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00160"><he>עֲדַק</he></cite>.]
Targ. Prov. XIX, 26 מְעָרֵיק (ed. Wil. מְעַרֵ׳; some ed. מַעֲרִיק Af.); a. e.
Targ. Jud. VI, 11 לעָרָקָא (ed. Wil. לַעֲרָ׳ Af.).
Targ. Job XLI, 20 יַעֲרִיק׳ (ed. יְעַרְק׳ Pa.).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 16:28">Targ. Prov. XVI, 28</cite> <he>מַעֲרִיק וכ׳</he> causes his friend to flee (him) (Var. <he>מעדיק</he>, v. <cite ref="P00160"><he>עֲדַק</he></cite>); a. e., v. supra.
